note.text: European colonial policies between 1900 and 1945 shared unequal imperial authority but differed across powers, regions and periods. Administration could rely more directly on officials or work through subordinated local rulers. Economic policies often sought revenue, labour and export production. Assimilation claimed incorporation into the coloniser's institutions and culture; association emphasised governing through distinctions and selected local arrangements. Neither label should be taken as a complete description of every colonial practice or as proof of equal rights.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: European colonial policies between {1900} and {1945} shared unequal imperial authority but differed across powers, regions and periods. Administration could rely more directly on officials or work through subordinated local rulers. Economic policies often sought revenue, labour and export production. Assimilation claimed incorporation into the coloniser's institutions and culture; association emphasised governing through distinctions and selected local arrangements. Neither label should be taken as a complete description of every colonial practice or as proof of equal rights.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: A French policy label, a British indirect-rule description and a plantation labour record answer different questions. Compare the intended model with how authority was exercised. A colonial official's promise of respect for custom may coexist with the power to depose a ruler or redirect local institutions.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Compare political structure, economic demands and social policy separately. Note differences and common imperial inequality. Avoid treating all policies as identical, or using a national label as evidence that every locality followed one unchanging system.
